doc_description: SEC Form 10-K for Best Buy Co., Inc. (NYSE: BBY) for the fiscal year ended January 28, 2023, detailing its U.S./Canada omnichannel electronics business (Domestic and International segments including Best Buy Health), FY2023 results (revenue $46.3B; comparable sales −9.9%), store footprint (978 U.S./160 Canada), FY22 acquisitions (Current Health, Yardbird), capital returns (dividend raised to $0.92; $1.0B buybacks under a $5.0B authorization), key risks (vendor concentration and reliance on branded credit cards), ESG goals (carbon neutral by 2040), and Deloitte-audited financials with effective ICFR.

structure.title: Preface
structure.summary:
- SEC Form 10-K filing for Best Buy Co., Inc. (fiscal year ended January 28, 2023), including registrant information, NYSE listing (BBY), filer status (well-known seasoned issuer; large accelerated filer), Section 404(b) ICFR attestation, market value of non-affiliate equity as of July 29, 2022, and shares outstanding as of March 15, 2023.
- Indications of reporting compliance (Exchange Act filings and Interactive Data Files), and that the company is not a shell company.
- Documents incorporated by reference: portions of the 2023 Definitive Proxy Statement for Part III.
- Safe harbor cautionary statement for forward-looking statements under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995.
- Table of Contents outlining Parts I–IV, including Business, Risk Factors, MD&A, Market Risk, Financial Statements, Controls and Procedures, and other standard 10-K items.
- Item 1. Business: Company overview—incorporated in Minnesota (1966); purpose to enrich lives through technology; vision to personalize and humanize technology solutions; operations in the U.S. and Canada.
- Reportable segments: Domestic (U.S. and Best Buy Health) and International (Canada). Domestic brands and domains include Best Buy, Best Buy Ads, Best Buy Business, Best Buy Health, CST, Current Health, Geek Squad, Lively, Magnolia, Pacific Kitchen and Home, TechLiquidators, Yardbird, and related websites; International brands include Best Buy, Best Buy Mobile, Geek Squad, and bestbuy.ca. Mexico stores closed by end of Q1 FY22.
- Recent acquisitions (FY22): Current Health Ltd. and Yardbird Furniture.
- Operations model: omnichannel platform (online, in-store, in-home); centrally managed merchandising, pricing, supply chain, digital, marketing, and support functions; standardized store procedures with localized flexibility; distinct leadership and operations for Best Buy Health supported by enterprise capabilities.
- Merchandise and services organized into six revenue categories:
  1) Computing and Mobile Phones (computers, peripherals, mobile, networking, tablets, wearables),
  2) Consumer Electronics (imaging, health/fitness, home theater, portable audio, smart home),
  3) Appliances (large and small),
  4) Entertainment (drones, gaming, media, toys, VR, software),
  5) Services (consultation, delivery, design, health services, installation, memberships, repair, setup, tech support, warranties),
  6) Other (baby, food/beverage, luggage, outdoor living, sporting goods).

structure.heading: PART I

Unless the context otherwise requires, the terms “we,” “us” and “our” in this Annual Report on Form 10-K refer to Best Buy Co., Inc. and, as applicable, its 
consolidated subsidiaries.
structure.summary:
- Section covered: Part I, Item 1. Business from Best Buy Co., Inc.’s Form 10-K, including definitional notes (use of “we/us/our”) and that website references are not incorporated by reference.
- Company overview: Incorporated in Minnesota in 1966; purpose is to enrich lives through technology; vision to personalize and humanize technology solutions for every stage of life; operates in the U.S. and Canada via an omnichannel model (online, in-store, in-home).
- Segments:
  - Domestic: U.S. operations plus Best Buy Health; brands include Best Buy, Best Buy Ads, Best Buy Business, Best Buy Health, CST, Current Health, Geek Squad, Lively, Magnolia, Pacific Kitchen and Home, TechLiquidators, and Yardbird; domains include bestbuy.com, currenthealth.com, lively.com, techliquidators.com, yardbird.com.
  - International: Canada operations under Best Buy, Best Buy Mobile, and Geek Squad; domain bestbuy.ca. All Mexico stores closed by end of Q1 fiscal 2022.
- Recent acquisitions (fiscal 2022): Current Health Ltd. and Two Peaks, LLC d/b/a Yardbird Furniture.
- Operations and management:
  - Both segments run an omnichannel platform.
  - Centralized management of merchandising and services development, pricing/promotions, procurement and supply chain, digital/app operations, marketing/advertising, and labor deployment; corporate support functions (HR, finance, IT, real estate) at headquarters.
  - Field operations support retail, services, and in-home teams; stores use standardized procedures with local flexibility; strategic decisions (locations, formats, assortments, fulfillment) handled at market/region level.
  - Best Buy Health has dedicated leadership and operations, with support from enterprise capabilities.
- Revenue categories (six) and key components:
  - Computing & Mobile Phones: desktops, notebooks, peripherals, mobile phones (incl. carrier commissions), networking, tablets/e-readers, wearables.
  - Consumer Electronics: digital imaging, health/fitness products, home theater, portable audio (headphones/speakers), smart home.
  - Appliances: large (dishwashers, laundry, ovens, refrigerators) and small (blenders, coffee makers, vacuums).
  - Entertainment: drones, gaming (hardware, peripherals, software), movies, music, toys, virtual reality, other software.
  - Services: consultation, delivery, design, health-related services, installation, memberships, repair, setup, technical support, warranty-related services.
  - Other: baby, food & beverage, luggage, outdoor living, sporting goods.

structure.title: Business.
structure.heading: Item 1. Business.
structure.start_phrase: Unless the context otherwise requires, the terms “we,” “us” and “our” in this Annual Report on Form 10-K refer to Best Buy Co., Inc. and, as applicable, its consolidated subsidiaries.
structure.summary:
- Overview and purpose: Best Buy Co., Inc., incorporated in Minnesota in 1966, operates to enrich lives through technology with an omnichannel model serving customers online, in stores, and in homes across the U.S. and Canada.
- Segments and brands: Two reportable segments:
  - Domestic (U.S. plus Best Buy Health) with brands including Best Buy, Best Buy Ads, Best Buy Business, Best Buy Health, CST, Current Health, Geek Squad, Lively, Magnolia, Pacific Kitchen and Home, TechLiquidators, Yardbird; domains such as bestbuy.com, currenthealth.com, lively.com, techliquidators.com, yardbird.com.
  - International (Canada) under Best Buy, Best Buy Mobile, Geek Squad; domain bestbuy.ca. Mexico stores closed in fiscal 2022.
  - Fiscal 2022 acquisitions: Current Health Ltd. and Yardbird Furniture.
- Operations: Centrally managed merchandising, pricing/promotions, procurement/supply chain, digital channels, marketing, and corporate support; standardized store procedures with local flexibility; dedicated leadership and operations for Best Buy Health.
- Offerings: Six revenue categories:
  - Computing & Mobile Phones
  - Consumer Electronics
  - Appliances
  - Entertainment
  - Services (consultation, delivery, design, health-related services, installation, memberships, repair, setup, tech support, warranties)
  - Other (baby, food/beverage, luggage, outdoor living, sporting goods)
- Distribution: Options include store pickup (including curbside), alternative pickup locations, and home delivery; ship-from-store capability; most goods flow manufacturer-to-DC.
- Suppliers and inventory: Vendor concentration—top 20 suppliers = ~79% of purchases; Apple, Samsung, HP, LG, Sony = ~57%. Generally no long-term supply contracts. Active inventory management with demand monitoring, vendor funding for markdowns/incentives, and return privileges. Global sourcing for exclusive brands.
- Store development: 1,138 stores at fiscal 2023 year-end; stores are core to omnichannel strategy; vendor store-within-a-store concepts; ongoing space optimization, lease renegotiations, selective openings/closures.
- Intellectual property: Extensive trademarks and service marks (e.g., Best Buy, Geek Squad, Insignia, Lively, Magnolia, Yardbird, Yellow Tag logo) and patents viewed as important marketing assets.
- Seasonality and working capital: Heavily weighted to fiscal Q4 holiday season; operations funded by cash, operating cash flow, and revolving credit facilities; seasonal inventory build before holidays.
- Competition: Competes with multi-channel retailers, e-commerce players, tech service providers, traditional retailers, vendors, and mobile carriers. Emphasis on price competitiveness and price matching; advantages include knowledgeable staff, integrated online/retail/in-home assets, curated assortment, vendor partnerships, services, experiential store formats, and supply chain.
- Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) oversight: Board committee oversees ESG strategy, risks, and public policy.
  - Environmental: Focus on circular economy, resource conservation, waste reduction, sustainable products, and renewable energy; investments in five solar fields. Goals include:
    - Reduce carbon emissions 75% by 2030 (vs. 2009) and reach carbon neutrality by 2040 via efficiency, renewable energy, fleet electrification, and offsets.
    - Reduce water consumption 15% by 2025 (vs. 2019).
    - Expand zero-waste certification in distribution centers.
    - Help customers reduce emissions 20% by 2030 (vs. 2017) via ENERGY STAR products, saving an estimated $5B in utility bills.
    - Recycling program collected 2.7B+ pounds since 2009 (183M in fiscal 2023).
  - Social—Human rights and sourcing: Alignment with UN Guiding Principles; Responsible Sourcing Program; membership in Responsible Business Alliance with shared Supplier Code of Conduct and audits.
  - Community impact: Best Buy Foundation supports 52 Teen Tech Center locations (goal: 100 by 2025), offering technology access, training, post-secondary guidance, mentors, mental health resources, and paid internships.
  - Human capital: ~90,000 employees in U.S. and Canada (58% full-time, 32% part-time, 10% seasonal). DEI progress toward 2025 goals: 37% of new salaried corporate roles filled by BIPOC; 25% of new salaried field roles filled by women. Commitments include $1.2B spend with BIPOC/diverse suppliers by 2025; up to $10M investment with Brown Venture Group; $44M by 2025 for BIPOC student opportunities and scholarships. Board oversight of HR policies and diversity.
  - Training and development: Average 44+ hours per U.S. employee in fiscal 2023; expanded leadership programs; AI-enabled workforce planning; LinkedIn Learning access; revamped onboarding.
  - Employee benefits: Enhanced caregiver support (Joshin, Wellthy), paid leave and caregiver pay, maternity leave up to 10 weeks at 100% pay, Included Health (LGBTQ+ support), virtual health visits, HOPE Fund emergency grants up to $2,500, mental health initiatives, and tuition assistance with potential zero out-of-pocket options.
- Public disclosures: SEC filings and governance documents available on investor website; SEC website access; corporate and investor sites used for broad public disclosure (not incorporated by reference).
- Risk Factors introduction: Outlines categories (external, strategic, operational, regulatory/legal, financial/market), notes potential for material adverse effects on performance and valuation, emphasizes non-exhaustive nature and qualifies forward-looking statements.

structure.title: Risk Factors.
structure.heading: Item 1A. Risk Factors.
structure.start_phrase: Described below are certain risks we believe apply to our business and the industry in which we operate.
structure.summary:
- Human capital initiatives and oversight: Mental health awareness and training; expanded tuition assistance with partner schools for no out-of-pocket costs; Board Compensation and Human Resources Committee oversight of wellness, engagement, benefit plan compliance, succession planning, and wage/retention/hiring programs.
- ESG and investor information: Reference to Best Buy’s Fiscal 2023 ESG Report (with TCFD index) to be published on the corporate sustainability site; availability of SEC filings and corporate governance documents on the investor website and by mail; website and social media used for public disclosures, not incorporated by reference.
- Risk Factors overview (External, Strategic, Operational, Regulatory/Legal, Financial/Market):
  - External: Macroeconomic pressures (inflation, recession risks, consumer confidence, bank liquidity), geopolitical tensions (Ukraine conflict; China/Taiwan) affecting supply chains and input costs; catastrophic events (climate-related disasters, pandemics including COVID-19, civil unrest) disrupting operations; rapid technology shifts and changing consumer preferences.
  - Strategic: Intense competition and price transparency; delivery speed/cost expectations; talent attraction/retention and rising wages/benefits; expansion into health and new offerings brings regulatory (e.g., FDA), privacy/security (HIPAA, GDPR) and execution risks; services model risks (attachment rates, Totaltech margin pressure, third-party quality, in-home liabilities); dependence on key vendors and mobile carriers (20 largest suppliers ~79% of merchandise; five vendors ~57%: Apple, Samsung, HP, LG, Sony); brand reputation; risks from ventures/acquisitions; real estate portfolio and lease commitments.
  - Operational: Store/supply chain interruptions (capacity, labor, transportation, theft/organized retail crime); reliance on third-party providers for critical functions; exclusive brands risks (Asia-based manufacturing, recalls, IP, tariffs, quality); challenges sourcing outside the U.S.; IT system dependence and cloud migration risks; heightened cybersecurity/online capacity and remote-work exposure; data privacy/security breach impacts and rising compliance costs; product safety/recalls; evolving labor/employment laws (unions, classification, wage/leave rules).
  - Regulatory and Legal: Complex, evolving laws (environmental, product compliance, privacy, labor, tax, trade/tariffs—especially with China) and litigation exposure; growing ESG disclosure expectations, costs, and reputational risks; climate change impacts; international operations risks (political, economic, FX, trade rules, cultural and labor differences, IP enforcement).
  - Financial/Market: Cost management pressures; heavy reliance on fiscal Q4/holiday season; promotional financing/co-brand card program performance (about 25% of FY2023 revenue on branded cards) sensitive to interest rates, credit losses, regulation; liquidity and vendor credit term risks; dependence on banks for cash access; credit rating changes; potential stock price impact from missing guidance.
- Item 1B: No unresolved SEC staff comments.

structure.title: Unresolved Staf f Comments.
structure.heading: Item 1B. Unresolved Staf f Comments.
structure.start_phrase: Not applicable.
structure.summary:
- Promotional financing risk: The company offers promotional financing and branded credit cards through third-party banks. About 25% of fiscal 2023 revenue was transacted on these cards. Profit-sharing income (and potential losses) depends on transaction volume, financing terms, bad debt, interest rates, regulatory and competitive factors, and program operating costs. Adverse changes could reduce the ability to offer attractive financing, depress sales, and diminish profit-share income.

- Liquidity risk: Operations rely on cash from operations, cash and liquid investments, credit facilities, other debt, and trade payables. Liquidity could be hurt by tighter vendor payment terms or credit limits. The company may need additional financing if existing sources are insufficient and depends on banks to safeguard and provide access to cash and short-term investments. Future liquidity is influenced by economic/market conditions, bank stability and regulation, credit availability, credit ratings, and lender perceptions, affecting borrowing costs, ability to pursue opportunities, and meeting obligations.

- Credit ratings risk: Downgrades or changes to ratings can restrict access to capital, increase borrowing costs, and worsen vendor and lease terms. Ratings can be revised, suspended, or withdrawn at any time, including due to new methodologies outside the company’s control.

- Guidance/stock price risk: Failure to meet or a reduction in financial guidance can lead to a stock price decline. Forecasting growth and margins is challenging; expenses and investments include significant fixed components that may not adjust quickly if sales lag. Revenue growth may slow and depends on product/service demand and global economic conditions.

- Item 1B—Unresolved Staff Comments: None.

structure.title: Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations.
structure.heading: Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations.
structure.start_phrase: Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (“MD&A”) is intended to provide a reader of our financial statements with a narrative from the perspective of our management on our financial condition, results of operations, liquidity and certain other factors that may af fect our future results.
structure.summary:
- Purpose and context of MD&A: Management provides narrative analysis of financial condition, results of operations, liquidity, and other factors; readers are directed to the consolidated financial statements (Item 8) and prior-year MD&A. The company operates on a 52-week fiscal year ending near end of January and experiences strong seasonality in Q4.

- Company overview and segments: U.S. and Canada operations with two reportable segments—Domestic (including Best Buy, Best Buy Health, Geek Squad, Yardbird, etc.) and International (Canada). Fiscal 2023 digital sales were 33% of Domestic revenue; stores remain central with 67% of revenue transacted in-store and significant cross-channel engagement.

- Comparable sales metric: Definition covers stores, websites, and call centers open at least 14 months; includes online sales, credit card revenue, gift card breakage, commercial/wholesale sales; excludes stores closed >14 days until 14 months after reopening, discontinued operations, services plan profit-share revenue, and FX effects (International). Recent acquisitions (Current Health, Yardbird) excluded from comps until Q1 FY2024.

- Non-GAAP financial measures: Use of constant currency, non-GAAP operating income, effective tax rate, and diluted EPS to supplement GAAP; typical adjustments include restructuring, impairments, settlements, investment gains/losses, intangible amortization, and acquisition costs; reconciliations provided.

- Business strategy update: Continued execution in a challenging environment; focus on omnichannel evolution (store portfolio, operating model, digital tools), membership growth (My Best Buy and paid Totaltech), and Best Buy Health (Care at Home) leveraging Geek Squad. Anticipates near-term industry sales declines amid inflation and rate pressures but expects longer-term growth from product replacement cycles, vendor innovation, and macro tech trends; expanding into newer categories (wellness tech, e-transportation, outdoor living, EV charging).

- Consolidated FY2023 results:
  - Revenue $46.3B, down 10.6%; comparable sales -9.9%.
  - Gross profit $9.9B (21.4% of revenue vs. 22.5% prior year).
  - SG&A $8.0B (17.2% of revenue vs. 16.7% prior year).
  - Operating income $1.8B (3.9% margin); net earnings $1.4B; diluted EPS $6.29.
  - Declines reflect lapping pandemic-driven demand/stimulus, consumer shift to services/experiences, and macro pressures.

- Domestic segment:
  - Revenue $42.8B, down 10.5%; comps -10.3%; online revenue $14.2B (33.2% of segment), comparable online sales -13.5%.
  - Category comps: Computing & Mobile -12.0%; Consumer Electronics -12.2%; Appliances -5.7%; Entertainment -5.5%; Services -2.5% (impacted by Totaltech bundling previously stand-alone services).
  - Margin drivers: Lower product and services margins (promotions, Totaltech benefits/costs), higher supply chain costs; partially offset by higher credit card profit-share and ~$30M services-plan profit-sharing benefit.
  - SG&A down due to ~ $455M lower short-term incentive expense and reduced store payroll.
  - Restructuring charges $140M tied to company-wide cost alignment initiative.
  - Store footprint: Ended FY2023 with 978 Domestic stores (925 Best Buy, 19 Outlet Centers, 20 Pacific Sales, 14 Yardbird). FY2024 plan: close ~20–30 Best Buy stores; increase Outlet Centers to ~30.

- International segment (Canada):
  - Revenue $3.5B, down 10.9%; comps -5.4%; FX unfavorable.
  - Category comps: Computing & Mobile -6.1%; Consumer Electronics -6.2%; Appliances +0.3%; Entertainment -8.6%; Services -2.1%.
  - Margin drivers: Lower product margins and higher supply chain costs; SG&A decreased on lower incentives and favorable FX.
  - Restructuring charges $7M; operating income margin decreased to 4.6%.
  - Store count stable at 160 (Canada Best Buy 127; Best Buy Mobile 33).

- Taxes and Non-GAAP:
  - Effective tax rate increased to 20.7% on reduced discrete benefits; non-GAAP ETR 21.0%.
  - Non-GAAP operating income $2.03B (4.4% margin) vs. $3.09B prior year; non-GAAP diluted EPS $7.08, down mainly on lower operating income.

- Liquidity and capital resources:
  - Cash and equivalents $1.87B (down from $2.94B) driven by share repurchases, capex, and dividends; partially offset by operating cash flow.
  - FY2023 cash flows: Operating $1.82B; Investing $(0.96)B; Financing $(1.81)B.
  - Revolving credit facility: $1.25B unsecured, expires May 2026; no borrowings outstanding; in compliance with covenants.
  - Credit ratings: S&P BBB+ (Stable); Moody’s A3 (Stable).
  - Restricted cash $379M (mainly for Totaltech product protection and self-insurance).
  - Capex $930M (IT/e-commerce $540M; stores $355M; supply chain $35M); FY2024 capex expected ~ $850M.
  - Debt outstanding: $500M notes due 2028; $650M notes due 2030.
  - Capital returns: FY2023 share repurchases $1.00B (11.8M shares at $84.78 avg); dividends $789M ($3.52 per share); announced 5% quarterly dividend increase to $0.92/share on March 2, 2023.
  - Other measures: Current ratio 1.0; debt-to-earnings 0.8 (from 0.5) on lower net earnings.
  - Contractual obligations total $7.56B (purchase obligations, leases, debt, interest, finance leases); $1.25B undrawn revolver capacity.

- Critical accounting estimates and sensitivities:
  - Vendor allowances: Complex classification and timing; a 10% change in deferral impacts net earnings by ~ $45M.
  - Goodwill: Two reporting units (Best Buy Domestic $492M; Best Buy Health $891M); fair values exceed book, with higher impairment risk for Health given market uncertainties.
  - Inventory markdowns: Estimation of net realizable value; a 10% change in markdown adjustment affects net earnings by ~ $14M.
  - Tax contingencies: Judgments on uncertain tax positions; outcomes could materially impact effective tax rate and cash.
  - Service revenue (memberships): Allocation/recognition judgments and usage estimates; a 10% change in deferred membership revenue affects net earnings by ~ $40M.

- Market risk—interest rates:
  - Net exposure: $1.8B (cash and restricted cash of $2.3B offset by $500M of debt swapped to floating).
  - Sensitivity: +/-50 bps in short-term rates changes net interest expense by ∓$9M.

structure.title: Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk.
structure.heading: Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk.
structure.start_phrase: In addition to the risks inherent in our operations, we are exposed to certain market risks.
structure.summary:
- Unrecognized tax benefits: Management’s estimates involve significant judgment and uncertainty due to changing tax laws, interpretations, timing, and internal factors like jurisdictional earnings and transaction timing. Outcomes differing from assumptions could materially affect the effective tax rate and cash flows; settlements (favorable or unfavorable) would impact the period’s tax rate. See Note 11 for details.
- Service revenue recognition: Membership plans (e.g., technical support, delivery/installation, discounts, protection plans, anti-virus) are accounted for by allocating transaction price to performance obligations based on relative fair value. Revenue for time-based obligations is recognized using a usage-based input method informed by historical patterns; when history is insufficient, recognition is ratable over the contract term. Key judgments include estimating standalone selling prices, selecting recognition methods, and forecasting usage. Sensitivity: a 10% change in deferred revenue as of Jan 28, 2023 would change fiscal 2023 net earnings by about $40 million. Deferred revenue has risen with the national launch of Best Buy Totaltech.
- New accounting standards: No recently issued pronouncements are expected to have a material effect.
- Market risk:
  - Interest rates: With $2.3 billion in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, and $500 million of fixed-rate debt swapped to floating (net $1.8 billion exposure), a 50 bps increase would reduce net interest expense by about $9 million; a 50 bps decrease would increase it by about $9 million. See Notes 6 and 8.
  - Foreign currency: Limited use of FX forwards to hedge inventory, receivables/payables, and the Canadian net investment. FY2023 USD strength vs. CAD reduced revenue by approximately $162 million; impact on net earnings was not significant. See Note 6.
- Management’s responsibility and audit: Management prepared the consolidated financial statements in conformity with GAAP, involving estimates and judgments. Deloitte & Touche LLP audited the statements under PCAOB standards and opined they present fairly, in all material respects, the company’s financial position, results, and cash flows in accordance with GAAP.
- Internal control over financial reporting: Designed to provide reasonable assurance over reliable reporting and safeguarding of assets, acknowledging inherent limitations. Using COSO 2013 criteria, management concluded ICFR was effective as of Jan 28, 2023, with no material weaknesses. Deloitte issued an unqualified attestation on ICFR.

structure.title: Financial Statements and Supplementary Data.
structure.heading: Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data.
structure.start_phrase: Our management is responsible for the preparation, integrity and objectivity of the accompanying consolidated financial statements and the related financial information.
structure.summary:
- Scope: Item 8 of Best Buy Co., Inc.’s Form 10-K, presenting audited consolidated financial statements, management’s responsibility statements, auditors’ reports, and detailed notes on accounting policies, operations, and risks for fiscal year ended January 28, 2023.

- Management’s reports:
  - Responsibility for preparing GAAP-compliant financial statements using estimates and judgments; consistency of related financial information in the 10-K.
  - Internal Control over Financial Reporting (ICFR) assessed under COSO 2013; concluded effective as of January 28, 2023; no material weaknesses identified.

- Independent auditor (Deloitte & Touche LLP):
  - Unqualified opinion on the consolidated financial statements for FY2021–FY2023 and on ICFR as of Jan 28, 2023; audits conducted under PCAOB standards; firm independent and serving since 2005.
  - Critical Audit Matters:
    - Vendor allowances: complexity due to volume/diversity of vendor agreements and timing/deferral; tested controls, recalculated amounts, confirmed terms, and assessed deferrals against inventory.
    - Goodwill impairment (Best Buy Health reporting unit): fair value via DCF with significant judgments (revenue growth, WACC); involved fair value specialists; no impairment recorded.

- Consolidated financial highlights (FY2023 vs FY2022):
  - Balance sheet: Total assets $15.8B (down from $17.5B); cash and cash equivalents $1.87B; inventories $5.14B; goodwill $1.38B; total equity $2.80B; long-term debt $1.16B; operating lease assets $2.75B.
  - Earnings: Revenue $46.3B (down from $51.8B); gross profit $9.91B; operating income $1.80B; net earnings $1.42B; diluted EPS $6.29 (from $9.84).
  - Cash flows: Operating cash flow $1.82B; investing cash outflow $0.96B (capex heavy); financing cash outflow $1.81B (share repurchases and dividends).

- Key notes to financial statements:
  - Business and segments: Two reportable segments—Domestic (includes Best Buy Health) and International (Canada); U.S. and Canada operations, Mexico exited in FY2022.
  - Significant accounting policies: GAAP basis; estimates; inventory at lower of cost or NRV (weighted-average, markdowns, physical loss); revenue recognition across products/services (principal vs agent), memberships, extended warranties (agent), credit card profit-share, gift cards/breakage, loyalty programs; leases (ASC 842); goodwill and intangibles impairment testing; fair value hierarchy; derivatives; income taxes.
  - Acquisitions (FY2022): Current Health ($389M; $351M goodwill to Best Buy Health) and Yardbird ($79M; $47M goodwill to Domestic); both not material to results.
  - Restructuring:
    - FY2023 Resource Optimization Initiative: $147M charges (primarily termination benefits; Domestic $140M, International $5M); remaining FY2024 charges not expected to be material.
    - Mexico exit and strategic realignment (FY2021–FY2022): cumulative charges primarily in International; stores in Mexico closed by Q1 FY2022.
  - Goodwill and intangibles: Total goodwill gross $2.06B with $0.68B cumulative impairment (International fully impaired previously); balances at 1/28/23—Domestic $1.45B (with $67M impairment), International $0; no new impairments. Definite-lived intangibles gross $532M; amortization expense $86M; weighted-average remaining life 7.2 years.
  - Fair value: Recurring L1/L2 positions (money market funds, time deposits, deferred comp investments, swaps); long-term debt fair value below carrying; nonrecurring measures tied to prior Mexico exit.
  - Derivatives: Net investment hedges (CAD), interest rate swaps on 2028 Notes (accounted for as fair value hedges via shortcut method; no P&L impact), FX forwards not designated for certain balances.
  - Leases: Operating lease assets $2.75B; total lease cost $1.02B; future operating lease payments undiscounted $3.03B; weighted average remaining term ~5.1 years.
  - Debt and liquidity:
    - Revolving credit facility: $1.25B unsecured, expires May 2026; no borrowings outstanding.
    - Notes: $500M 2028 Notes (4.45%); $650M 2030 Notes (1.95%); no maturities within next five fiscal years; swap valuation adjustments flow through carrying value.
  - Shareholders’ equity:
    - Stock-based compensation expense $138M (time-, performance-, and market-based awards; minimal options activity).
    - Share repurchases: $1.00B in FY2023 (11.8M shares at avg $84.78); $4.125B remaining under $5.0B authorization at year-end; dividends paid $790M (~$3.52/share).
    - EPS calculations and dilutive securities noted.
  - Revenue details:
    - Contract balances: gift cards, deferred revenue, loyalty; revenue recognized from opening contract liabilities disclosed; multi-year revenue recognition schedule for longer-term obligations.
    - Domestic product category revenue (FY2023): Computing/Mobile $18.2B; Consumer Electronics $13.0B; Appliances $6.4B; Entertainment $2.8B; Services $2.1B.
  - Income taxes: Effective tax rate 20.7%; deferred tax assets/liabilities detailed; valuation allowance $150M; unrecognized tax benefits $163M; IRA 2022 expected to be not material.
  - Benefit plans: 401(k) match $77M; non-qualified deferred comp plan (liability $20M).
  - Contingencies and commitments: Routine legal proceedings with appropriate accruals; letters of credit outstanding $72M.
  - Segment and geographic information:
    - FY2023 revenue: Domestic $42.8B; International $3.5B.
    - Operating income: Domestic $1.63B; International $0.16B.
    - Assets: Domestic $14.5B; International $1.25B.
    - Geographic revenue predominantly U.S. ($42.8B) and Canada ($3.5B).
